---
title: "Applied replication for data skills"
subtitle: "Housing and racial bias"
engine: knitr
format:
  live-revealjs:
    webr:
      # The packages that the helpers of the lab and the cells of the hands-on
      # slides call: dplyr and purrr in the helpers, parameters with sandwich
      # for the HC2 errors, marginaleffects for the logit and effectsize for
      # the conversion rule of the robustness study; datawizard in the cells of
      # Task 3. The runtime adds evaluate, knitr and htmltools itself, and
      # tibble comes with dplyr. The session has no graph task and no figure in
      # a cell, so tinyplot stays out, and gt is left out because no slide
      # prints a formatted table and it adds 12 to 23 seconds to the first
      # opening of a page.
      packages:
        - dplyr
        - datawizard
        - purrr
        - parameters
        - sandwich
        - marginaleffects
        - effectsize
# The four files that the cells read, fetched into the browser when the deck
# opens; the runtime drops the leading ../ of each path, so inside the browser
# they sit under data/, the folder that the setup cell below
# names as .data_dir.
resources:
  - ../data/housing_emails.csv
  - ../data/housing_original.csv
  - ../data/spec_curve.csv
  - ../data/menu_options.csv
live:
  show-hints: true
  show-solutions: true
# Optional runs that this deck includes in its main flow (core-runs.lua
# strips their .deepdive mark); the others stay on the d toggle. This deck
# carries one optional run, the multiverse background of the second half.
core-runs: []
# The format of the deck, which the segments of the Housing case study read
# through Quarto conditional content (when-meta="deck.short" and so on): one
# of short or day, and menu where the deck teaches the specification menu.
deck:
  short: true
  menu: true
# THE DECK OF THE SHORT FORMAT
# - The participants do every task of the session in this deck, whose
#   hands-on slides carry the cells of the browser lab through the Quarto
#   Live extension: Task 1 and its warm-up, Task 3 with each of the five
#   reproductions, Task 4 without the submission, and the placement. The
#   estimand statement of Task 2 is a held answer in the chat, and the
#   session sends nothing to the class chart and has no Task 5. The browser
#   lab, lab.qmd, stays the fallback.
# - The hands-on segments in _segments/ (_handson1-live.qmd,
#   _handson3-live.qmd, _handson4-live.qmd, _handson4-tries-live.qmd and
#   _placement-live.qmd) hold the cells of the lab, one step to a cell, with
#   the hints and solutions of its exercises. The helpers of the lab are
#   ../_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd, included after the setup cell that
#   names the data folder. The two setup segments stay in
#   ../slides/_segments/, because the decks of day 3 include them as well.
# - The setup cell and the helpers sit on the agenda slide, after its notes,
#   because a cell or a comment placed before the first heading of a deck
#   makes a slide of its own; they print nothing.
# - The half dividers keep the ids that the pages of the format link.
# - No duration goes on any slide or into any note.
---

```{webr}
# The setup of the deck, run once the engine is ready. .data_dir is the folder
# in which the four files of the resources list arrive inside the browser: the
# runtime drops the leading ../ of their paths, so from the working directory
# of R they sit under data/. housing holds the emails, one row
# each, the object from which the cells of the hands-on slides work.
.data_dir <- "data"
housing <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "housing_emails.csv"), na.strings = c("", "NA"))  # r-style: keep – the base reader adds nothing to the download
```
